rootCauseOfFailure.summary: The detailed-agreement gate fails not because the implemented fix was wrong, but because it was NECESSARY-BUT-INSUFFICIENT: it closed the specific 'action-signal-empty, weak-lexical-overlap' pathway it targeted (confirmed: zero regression, +3pp binary agreement, one concrete false-match eliminated), but a DIFFERENT, newly-diagnosed generalized mechanism - sibling/sub-clause identity discrimination within the same covenant family (16-remaining-evaluator-risks.json R3) - accounts for the majority of the remaining detailed disagreements and was not addressed because it was only clearly identified by analyzing THIS rerun's own results, after the pre-rerun freeze.
rootCauseOfFailure.diagnosisCategory: Per Section 29's required categories, this is primarily EVALUATOR_IMPLEMENTATION (R3: the safe-surfacing/partial-credit gate does not require sub-provision identity discrimination, and the live-judge call-routing policy never reconsiders a deterministic CORRESPONDS_PARTIALLY outcome), secondarily REVIEWER_PROTOCOL / INHERENT_AMBIGUITY (R5: the independent reviewer's complete non-use of 6 of 10 available labels across 42 cases is itself unusual and not conclusively distinguished from a genuine evaluator gap in this phase).
rootCauseOfFailure.notGtQuality: Not primarily a GT-quality problem: the 9 exclusions were mutually and independently agreed by both V2 and the fresh reviewer, and the disagreements analyzed in depth (R3, R4) trace to specific, real, well-drafted candidates that are genuinely ABOUT a different provision than the one they were credited against - not to garbled or ambiguous ground truth.
rootCauseOfFailure.notAnUnrealisticGate: Not a case for relaxing the gate definition: the detailed-agreement bar exists specifically to catch exactly this class of defect (confidently mislabeling WHICH representation state applies), and this rerun demonstrates the bar is doing its job - it caught a real, previously-undiagnosed, systemic defect (R3) that the binary-only view would have hidden entirely.

verdictJustification: Binary agreement (criterion 10) passes at 90.48%, a genuine, generalized, zero-regression improvement over Phase 3F.1.5.1's 87.5%. Detailed agreement (criterion 11) fails at 11.90%, against the required >=85%, and is WORSE than Phase 3F.1.5.1's 18.75% despite the phase's dedicated remediation - a specific, well-diagnosed, newly-discovered mechanism (R3: sibling/sub-clause identity discrimination) accounts for the majority of the shortfall. Per Section 28, ALL pass criteria must hold; criterion 11 does not. Per Section 29, this phase stops here rather than attempting a second patch within the same phase.

This report does not create that phase, begin it, or assume it will happen.
nextStepRecommendation.ifNoFurtherEvaluatorIterationIsAuthorize: Per Section 31 (which applies even on a NEEDS_ITERATION outcome, by the same product-outcome logic), the alternative to a third evaluator-calibration phase is to treat the CURRENT evaluator as accurate-enough-to-inform product decisions where its binary judgment is reliable (90.5% agreement) while treating its detailed safe-state labeling as not yet trustworthy for downstream product behavior that depends on distinguishing WHICH kind of gap exists - and to return to Headroom's own bounded residual foundation closure using the evidence already gathered, rather than open-endedly re-tuning the evaluator.
